title: Cloudflare recommended for supplier app hosting; recipient fulfillment remains a verification gate
summary: Deployment review found the existing Project DVito configuration already uses Workers static assets, D1, and Access configuration. Recommended architecture, pending owner adoption: Workers for UI/API, D1 for role-scoped application records, and a Durable Object per supplier wallet for durable spending coordination and scheduled renewals. Official alarm documentation guarantees at-least-once execution, so persisted attempt state and reconciliation must prevent repeat financial submissions; hosting alone cannot guarantee exactly-once upstream charges. Existing blueprint and handoff distinguish owner-reported wallet-funded recipient promos from independently verified integration. Build roles, persisted plans and forecast first; verify the precise payer-wallet/recipient-offer/delivery flow before enabling real automation. No deployment, login or financial action occurred, and no provider acceptance from Cloudflare was established.

evidence.description: Existing Cloudflare Workers, static assets, D1 and Access configuration; configuration does not verify current deployment health.
Agreed role model and outstanding integration requirements.
Workers supports frontend assets and backend API hosting.
Managed SQL storage for application records.
Persisted schedules and at-least-once execution with retries require application-level duplicate protection.

nextSteps: Build an isolated staging app with authenticated roles, durable records and simulated fulfillment before production spending.
Verify recipient eligibility, supplier-wallet debit route and recipient delivery evidence through separately authorized provider experiments.
Persist submission intent before external calls; reconcile uncertain outcomes and block duplicate submission across alarm retries.
